props.note: Poseidon composite carbonate edifice: about 60 m tall and 100 m across (Denny et al. 2016, Geologic evolution of Lost City). Width and depth describe the full group of adjoining spires and foundation, not one column. The 100 m depth is a build footprint, not a measured plan outline. Snapped to the same terrain-matched terrace as before; internal layout and heading are scenic. Clear-fluid shimmer comes from the mission vent preset, with smoke and glow disabled. See sources.md.

Beehive was a roughly 1 m parasitic vent on Poseidon (Denny et al. 2016); Aquino et al. 2024 report that its chimney was absent in 2018. This separately scannable marker is illustrative and offset from Poseidon, not a claim that the historical structure survives or stood here.

IMAX is a parasitic flange and chimney on Poseidon's north face. Kelley et al. 2005 report ~8 m; Denny et al. 2016 describe a ~30 m multipronged structure. This 8 m separate marker is illustrative; its offset position is for scanning and not a surveyed footprint.

Illustrative minor chimney; the field has dozens of spires and flanges of varying size (Kelley et al. 2005 describe a dense cluster), most unnamed and unmapped individually. Height and position are invented.
Illustrative minor chimney (see unnamed-chimney-1). Height and position are invented.
Unnamed carbonate spire in the wider field; the field has dozens of towers and flanges (Kelley et al. 2005). Height and position are scenic, behind Poseidon.
